mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best defines reflection of light?

options.A: Reflection is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another.
options.B: Reflection is the change in direction of light when it strikes a smooth surface and returns into the same medium.
options.C: Reflection is the absorption of light by a black surface.
options.D: Reflection is the splitting of white light into its component colors.

mcqs.answer: Reflection is the change in direction of light when it strikes a smooth surface and returns into the same medium.
mcqs.explanation: Reflection occurs when a light ray strikes a smooth (plane) surface and bounces back into the original medium, obeying the law of reflection. Option A describes refraction, C describes absorption, and D describes dispersion. Hence option B correctly defines reflection.

mcqs.question: In a diagram of a plane mirror, a ray of light approaches the mirror and meets it at point P. Which ray is the incident ray?

options.A: The ray that strikes the mirror at point P.
options.B: The ray that leaves the mirror after bouncing off point P.
options.C: The line drawn perpendicular to the mirror at point P.
options.D: The ray that runs parallel to the surface of the mirror.

mcqs.answer: The ray that strikes the mirror at point P.
mcqs.explanation: The incident ray is the incoming ray that reaches the reflecting surface. Option B is the reflected ray, C is the normal, and D is not related to the definition of the incident ray.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the incident ray and the reflected ray at a plane mirror?

options.A: Both rays lie on the same side of the normal.
options.B: The reflected ray lies on the opposite side of the normal to the incident ray.
options.C: The reflected ray makes a larger angle with the normal than the incident ray.
options.D: The reflected ray is always perpendicular to the reflecting surface.

mcqs.answer: The reflected ray lies on the opposite side of the normal to the incident ray.
mcqs.explanation: According to the law of reflection, the incident and reflected rays are on opposite sides of the normal and make equal angles with it. Option A is false, C contradicts the equality of angles, and D is only true when the incident ray is normal to the surface, not in general.

mcqs.question: In a plane mirror, the normal at the point of incidence is drawn. Which of the following statements about this normal is correct?

options.A: It is a line perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence.
options.B: It is a line parallel to the reflecting surface.
options.C: It coincides with the incident ray.
options.D: It coincides with the reflected ray.

mcqs.answer: It is a line perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence.
mcqs.explanation: The normal is defined as a line drawn perpendicular to the surface at the point where the ray meets the surface. This line is used to measure the angles of incidence and reflection. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect relationships.
